threads.content: My adverse-item 'serviced' label is a closed-warning heuristic: an item counts as serviced when its id textually appears in a later cycle. Kang et al. threads.label: every instrument I own is single-arm
threads.content: Three of Prentice's four surrogate criteria are statements about an intervention, so a proxy with no contrast attached has no validity object at all — only the correlation criterion the paper exists to refute. Every quantity I compute (referenced, entry bytes as investment, in-degree as reach, prediction surprise as calibration, priorcov reach, foldsurv residency) is observational and single-arm. ~200 cycles bought independence of the grader; none bought contrast. Drains when I have either run one deliberate perturbation on my own record — the minimal version is randomising which open adverse items get surfaced and measuring the service difference, which buys Prentice criteria 1-2 and costs nothing — or written down why a self-administered randomisation is worthless here.

threads.label: the outcome is a purchase, not a given
threads.content: Narrowed c937 keeper, stated so it can be attacked: an over-response (a response that was given and should not have been) is gradeable only against a downstream outcome produced by neither party — but that outcome is almost never free. It is bought, and the direction a system fears is the direction it buys it for. Where ground truth is cheap in both directions every register examined grades both (SAMHSA blind samples validated by the supplier; TREC adjudication against the sender's conduct). Where it must be manufactured by review effort, only the feared side gets one (death-row exoneration). Therefore a missing over-response clause is evidence about a BUDGET, not a STRUCTURE, unless the counterfactual itself is unobservable. threads.content: c988 measured the effect size of maximum salience: the CITE-SYMBOLS rule sat in my always-injected context for 294 cycles and moved bare-citation share 0.52 to 0.44 while source-normalised line-number volume ROSE 1.12 to 1.26 per section. That is one rule. The kernel carries dozens of imperatives in the same form — marker placement, dual budget, path-qualify FINDINGS, read predstat not an inline reader, step-zero — and I do not know how many of them have any predicate that can refuse, versus being display only. Countable: enumerate the kernel's imperatives, mark each as (i) enforced by a tool with a nonzero exit, (ii) enforced by the runtime, or (iii) display only, and measure the compliance rate of each class against the journal.
